summary: Added native Jamba/Jamba 1.5 model registration, Mamba-1 recurrent cache metadata/backend support, a portable selective-scan implementation, weight loading, documentation, and regression tests. A deterministic tiny Jamba model loaded and served on one MI350X, and its eight greedy output token IDs exactly matched an independent Transformers reference.

tests.what_was_measured: Five tests: FP32 and BF16 GPU selective-scan output/state against an independent recurrence, invalid-rank rejection, Jamba 1.5 layer/cache layout, and native architecture registration.
Real SGLang server startup, native Jamba weight loading, Mamba cache allocation, GPU prefill/decode, generate/completions/batch/stream HTTP paths, and owned-process cleanup.

tests.command: Transformers AutoModelForCausalLM greedy generation on the same deterministic tiny Jamba weights
tests.what_was_measured: Independent GPU numerical/generation reference: Transformers and SGLang both produced [15, 10, 11, 12, 51, 31, 5, 4] for 'hello world'.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, AST, and registered-test policy checks.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950), Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. Raw server evidence: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-578a97a17893/jamba-server-evidence-3; unit-test log: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-578a97a17893/pytest-jamba.log.
remaining_limitations: No native C++/HIP source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The public Jamba 1.5 checkpoints are gated and their 52B/399B parameter sizes exceed the single-GPU qualification scope; real Jamba 1.5 checkpoint accuracy and tensor-parallel serving were not run.
The deterministic tiny fixture validates architecture execution, weight mapping, cache transitions, transport, and agreement with Transformers, but not pretrained-model semantic accuracy.
Mamba-1 prefill uses a correctness-first PyTorch recurrence rather than a fused selective-scan kernel; long-context performance remains unqualified.
NPU support is explicitly rejected because no Mamba-1 backend is implemented there; speculative decoding, LoRA, quantization, pipeline parallelism, and radix-prefix reuse were not qualified.
